concerns.quote: The evidence revealed that in 2015, the Trust did not hold records of the training received by individual nurses. Instead, it was left to each individual nurse to maintain their own training records.

The evidence taken at the inquest revealed that despite the complex medical needs of this child, no formal written care plan was created for the period he was in hospital, from | September 2013 to January 2015 (15 months).
concerns.hazard: absence of formal written care plan

categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The inquest found there was a delay between the patient being found in an unresponsive condition and CPR being initiated
The lady working as a bank nurse in the Emergency Department (ED), who found the patient unresponsive, admitted to the Trust's investigator she was not familiar with the crash call system
concerns.hazard: lack of familiarity with crash call system

concerns.quote: The experienced nurse alerted to the situation also did not press the crash call buzzer
concerns.hazard: experienced nurse did not press crash call buzzer

concerns.quote: It is acknowledged that some additional refresher training has been carried out since this incident
concerns.hazard: lack of audit or verification of training

concerns.quote: It was unclear whether the Trust's contractual arrangements with nursing agencies stipulate the requirement for those supplied to (a) be professionally qualified (b) have current training to specified standards and (c) have undergone appropriate induction
concerns.hazard: uncertain agency staff qualifications and training requirements

links.explanation: Both reports concern the verification of nurses' training and qualifications. The earlier report highlights missing central training records, while the later report points out absent contractual requirements for agency nurses' training and induction.
links.earlier_quote: The evidence revealed that in 2015, the Trust did not hold records of the training received by individual nurses. Instead, it was left to each individual nurse to maintain their own training records.
links.later_quote: (9) It was unclear whether the Trust's contractual arrangements with nursing agencies stipulate the requirement for those supplied to (a) be professionally qualified (b) have current training to specified standards and (c) have undergone appropriate induction to the ED.
